To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
bacterial MreB forms filaments that associate with the cytoplasm membrane and that these filaments organize specific membrane domains with increased fluidity.
bacterial MreB filamens create membrane domains with increased fluidity, and that the Mreb cytoskeleton influences the localization of membrane proteins.

the bacterial actomyosin homologue MREB creates specific membrane regions that are enriched in fluid lipids (MreB-induced Fluid Lipid Regions, RIFs) and that these RIFs are important for the localization of membrane proteins.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the bacterial actin cytoskeletal protein MreB in bacterial membrane organization.
the bacterial cell envelope, the outermost structure of a cell, which is composed of the cell wall and the cell membrane.
the question how bacteria organize the cell membrane.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
MreB is a membrane organizer.
the bacterial acto-myosin cytoskeleton, in addition to its known function, is able to organize and control the bacterial cell membrane.
the bacterial acto-myosin-like cytoskeleton influences bacterial membrane organization and fluid lipid domains.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
MreB organises the cell membrane by generating membrane regions with increased lipid fluidity (Rif).
the bacterial actomyosin-like system is able to create membrane domains with specific lipid properties, comparable to eukaryotic membrane rafts.
the MreBs in the bacterial membrane create a fluid domain that is required for the proper localization of many membrane proteins.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the bacterial actomyosin system is a versatile tool to organize the bacterial cell membrane and to control the fluidity and distribution of membrane proteins.
MreB organises the bacterial cell membrane in a way similar to eukaryotic actin, which is a major player in eukaryotic membrane organisation.

the MreBLIP2 complex, which organizes the bacterial actin cytoskeletal network and coordinates cell wall synthesis, is also responsible for the creation of specific membrane domains that influence membrane protein distribution.
